html:
Around 130 BCE the Yuezhi, a nomad people driven out of western China, took over Bactria, the rich land on the upper Oxus river in today's Afghanistan, Uzbekistan and Tajikistan.

The Yuezhi had lived on the grasslands of Gansu, near the Hexi corridor. In the 170s and 160s BCE the Xiongnu under Modu and his son crushed them; Chinese sources say the Xiongnu ruler made a drinking cup from the Yuezhi king's skull. Most of the Yuezhi moved west, first to the Ili valley, then, pushed again by the Wusun, south to the Oxus.

There they overran the last of the Greco-Bactrian kingdom. The Chinese envoy Zhang Qian found them there around 128 BCE, settled and prosperous.

The Yuezhi split into five chiefdoms. In the 1st century CE one of them, the Kushan, under Kujula Kadphises, united the rest and built the Kushan Empire, which reached deep into India and helped carry Buddhism to China. Some scholars link the Yuezhi to the Tocharian speakers of the Tarim Basin, but this is debated.
sum: Around 130 BCE the Yuezhi, a nomad people driven out of western China, took over Bactria, the rich land on the upper Oxus river in today's Afghanistan, Uzbekistan and Tajikistan.
